subject: POC Playbook: success gates, hybrid eval approach & ownership map

Subject: POC Playbook: success gates, hybrid eval approach & ownership map

Hi Susan — thanks again for a productive discovery earlier today. This note captures our recommended POC approach, success gates, and immediate next steps so we have a shared playbook to operate from. I attached a one-page charter and an initial grading rubric (two attachments) — please confirm any missing constraints.

Summary of what we heard on the call
- Primary use case: automated triage + suggested response drafts for patient intake teams (EHR snippets + unstructured notes).
- Key success outcomes: 1) >= 85% precision on suggested triage category, 2) mean end-to-end turnaround (user request to suggested draft visible) < 1.2s p95 in shadow, 3) no PHI egress and KMS-based key control.

Recommended POC design (high level) — Hybrid evaluation path
1) Offline quality pass (3 weeks) — run Redwood on a historical dataset (10k de-identified records) and score outputs against your labeled set using the attached rubric. This focuses on label-level precision/recall and semantic safety checks.
2) Live shadow (2 weeks) — mirror live traffic in a read-only path to validate latency, inference routing, and KV-cache behavior. Outputs are not surfaced to patients. This validates operational SLOs and degradation behavior under burst.
3) Acceptance gate — both offline score thresholds and p95 latency SLOs must be met. If offline quality or latency is off, we iterate the model variant/quantization profile with a quick retest window (5 business days).

Owners & timeline (proposed)
- Commercial / owner: Me (Kimberly) — deal-level coordination, commercial artifacts.
- SE / technical lead: Ben Carter — proof-run setup, dataset ingestion, shadow routing config.
- Customer success / onboarding: Marissa Cole — data intake coordination and compliance checklist.
- Customer data owner: Susan Patel — provide labeled sample and point of contact for contracts/data access.

Immediate next steps (this week)
- Susan: confirm you can share the 10k de-identified sample and highlight any columns we should exclude (ETA: Wed 11/11).
- Contracts: if we need an NDA/data processing addendum, contracts@clearpathhealth.com to loop in (CC'd).
- Ben: I’d like a quick runbook for ingest (no PII) and an initial estimate for compute.

Attachments: clearpath-poc-charter.pdf (1p), eval-rubric-v1.xlsx (grading matrix), data-access-checklist.pdf (PII checklist).

Thanks — I’ll stand up a shared drive folder and HubSpot milestone when Susan confirms data availability.

Thanks — quick technical note on the evaluation methodology and the rubric (see attached eval-rubric-v1.xlsx for the spreadsheet):

Why hybrid (offline + shadow)?\- Offline lets us iterate quickly on prompt templates, temperature, and small model variants without impacting live traffic. It gives a reproducible, labeled-quality signal (precision/recall, semantic-safety checks).\- Shadow validates routing, caching, and latency under realistic fan-out and token distributions. It also surfaces edge-case tokenization/regeneration patterns that are hard to simulate with static samples.

Suggested offline grading rubric (summary)
- Triage precision (category match): pass if >= 0.85 (weight 40%)
- Suggested draft acceptability (human-review 3-point scale): average >= 2.5/3 (weight 30%)
- Safety blockers (PHI leakage / hallucination): zero critical failures allowed (weight 20%)
- Latency proxy (inference-only, offline): median < 0.6s (weight 10%)

Acceptance rule: weighted score >= 0.82 AND no safety blockers. If shadow p95 latency > 1.2s, put a pause on rollout and trigger a performance tuning cycle (we'll try different quantization profiles and kernel configs).

Telemetry for shadow (what we'll request) — short list you can hand to security:
- Request ID + anonymized request hash (no patient identifiers)
- Token-level timing traces (start, model queue wait, model exec, send)
- Aggregate token counts and peak concurrency windows
- Error rates and model fallback counts

I’ll also include a simple scoring script we can run inside your secure environment (so labeled data never leaves your VPC). If you prefer, we can run the offline quality pass in your VPC; that would remove data egress concerns but requires a short on-prem kit install.

—Ben

Quick CS note — we’re aligned on the hybrid route. A couple operational additions from onboarding:

- Access model: For shadow we’ll request an IAM role with read-only S3 access and temporary credentials via our onboarding portal. We will not copy raw records — only hashed request ids and derived features will be kept for analysis.
- Audit evidence: Susan, we’ll need a SOC2 evidence drop for ingestion controls; if you can point us to the right person on your InfoSec team we’ll kickoff the evidence request template.
- Rollback plan: If shadow uncovers a safety blocker, we’ll immediately remove the route and revert to a minimal-response model variant while remediation occurs.

I’ll create the onboarding runbook this afternoon and post to the shared folder.
